solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Kept destroyers at sea, to start with

indicators.note: being at sea means confused, so the letters taken are thrown into a new order
only the opening stretch of the word destroyers is used, its first six letters, the tail being dropped

explanation.surface: A naval report: warships were held back in reserve while out at sea, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start with' trims destroyers to its first six letters, DESTRO, and 'at sea' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods put away for later use have been kept in a store, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: See it's sewn, having been torn

indicators.note: something torn is ripped apart, so the letters of the two words are pulled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a garment: look, the seam has been stitched up after a rip.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in it's gives no letter; ITS and SEWN together are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness something is to see it happen, as an eyewitness does; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Are of minor importance for a host

definitions.meaning: things that matter less can be said to count for less, the two-word phrase read literally
a host of things is a vast number, too many to tally, so the adjective describes such a multitude

explanation.surface: Guests or hosts: a reflection on who matters less at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as COUNT LESS, the answer means 'matter less'; whole, it means innumerable, which is what 'a host' of things are.
explanation.definitionFit: A host means a great multitude, so numbers beyond reckoning; noun phrase standing for the adjective.

clue.text: Request best man to come inside

indicators.note: one piece is told to come inside the other, so the pronoun is placed within the word best

parts.note: taken as written
a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: An invitation asking the best man at a wedding to step indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is not the best man of the surface but a pronoun, and 'to come inside' places it within the word best.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or request made by someone, as in 'at my behest'.

clue.text: Pro French, is protected by conservationists?

parts.note: to be pro something is to be for it
the French word for 'is' is est

explanation.surface: A pro-French stance shielded by environmental campaigners.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: woodland is a typical thing conservationists protect.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodlands are classic habitats that environmental groups campaign to preserve, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Phoney, ludicrous tot's voice — high

parts.note: phoney means false or fake

indicators.note: something ludicrous is absurd and jumbled, so the little word's letters are shuffled

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter; just the three letters of tot are used

explanation.surface: A child putting on a fake, silly squeaky voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on tot's adds no letter, and 'ludicrous' rearranges the three letters; the definition runs across the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high singing register a male singer uses above his normal range.

clue.text: He abandoned her, due to having quarrelled

indicators.note: he abandoning her means the two letters of he leave the word her

parts.note: taken as written
money that is due is owed

explanation.surface: A man left his partner after a falling-out: a domestic drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' takes HE out of HER, leaving R.
explanation.definitionFit: A row, rhyming with cow, is a quarrel, so rowed means argued or fell out.

clue.text: Unruffled by incoming puff of air

indicators.note: the short word comes into the middle of the longer one

parts.note: unruffled means calm, serene
a puff is a promotional plug, an advertisement, abbreviated AD

explanation.surface: A calm person barely disturbed by a gust of breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'puff' looks like part of 'puff of air', but it is an advert; 'air' alone is the definition, a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a tune or melody, and a serenade is a song sung to a beloved.

clue.text: Having reached your destination, need to be picked up?

definitions.meaning: when the journey is finished, the travel is done and finished, the outing ended
someone who stumbles and falls may need helping back to their feet

explanation.surface: A traveller arriving somewhere and asking for a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase it is a journey ended; read as a verb it is to stumble, after which you might need lifting up.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumbling over something leaves you on the ground needing help up; a journey that is done is finished.

clue.text: Noisy, turns down — they're in the garden

parts.note: F stands for forte, the musical direction meaning loud
to turn down volume is to lower it

explanation.surface: Someone complaining about loud neighbours who switch off and retreat outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Blooms are the familiar contents of beds and borders, a definition by example.

clue.text: Keep talking of people rushing to buy

definitions.meaning: to carry on chattering past the point of stopping
a sudden demand for something, as on a bank or a product, when crowds hurry to purchase

explanation.surface: Chatter about shoppers stampeding for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A rush of demand for goods is called by this phrase, and to ramble on is the verb sense.

clue.text: Chopping finely and dropping right in

indicators.note: the letter for right is put in the longer word

parts.note: dropping, as leaves or hair, is shedding

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: cut finely and then tip the right ingredient in.
explanation.definitionFit: To shred is to cut into thin strips, as with cabbage or documents.

clue.text: The woman's taken about an hour to get back

indicators.note: getting back means going in the opposite direction, so the joined letters are read from the end

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A woman takes nearly an hour to return home.
explanation.walkthrough: RE followed by H, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun for a female person, belonging to her, matches the woman's.

clue.text: Does reform, dead miserable

indicators.note: to reform is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: A reformer who changes their ways, yet remains utterly gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reform' rearranges DOES as DESO.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means wretched and forlorn, a synonym for miserable.

clue.text: Being smart, endeavour to conceal intention

indicators.note: concealing something means keeping it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to endeavour is to try
an end is an aim or intention

explanation.surface: Advice on looking stylish while hiding your true motives.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashionable and stylish things are smart; an adjective synonym.

clue.text: Check and say 'Stet'

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
to say is to state

explanation.surface: An editor's instructions: verify the text and mark it to stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Stet is the proofreader's mark meaning 'let it stand', telling the printer to restore a deleted word.
explanation.definitionFit: The editor's mark tells the printer to restore struck-out wording, so it works as an imperative.

clue.text: Open with a number that is suggestive

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
one is a number

explanation.surface: Starting with a figure that hints at something racy.
explanation.definitionFit: An overtone is an implied hint or nuance, something that suggests more than it says.

clue.text: Mum, they lost the toss

parts.note: mum as in 'keep mum' means hush, and sh is the call for silence

indicators.note: the word they has lost the three letters spelling the

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother and her team ruefully losing the coin toss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the call for quiet; THE is taken from THEY, leaving Y.
explanation.definitionFit: To shy is to fling or throw something, as at a coconut shy.

clue.text: Group of animals commandeering foreground: English breed

indicators.note: commandeering means seizing and holding, so the group surrounds the letters

parts.note: a herd is a group of cattle or other animals
the clue seems to treat fore (the front) ground down as for; a loose device

explanation.surface: Livestock taking over the front of a scene: a pastoral painting of English cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: The device is loose: 'foreground' seems to mean fore ground down, losing its last letter, with English placed in front. Hereford is a beef cattle breed named after the English county of Herefordshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford is a well-known red and white beef cattle breed originating in Herefordshire.

clue.text: Dig a hole in, man!

indicators.note: the round letter is placed in the pronoun

parts.note: a man is he
O is a hole, from its shape

explanation.surface: Telling a workman to excavate a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoe is to break up or work the soil with a garden tool, a kind of digging.

clue.text: Against state having some secrets

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly

indicators.note: only some of the word secrets is used, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A country hostile to a regime with things to hide.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed to it, unwilling.

clue.text: A bossy boy expelled. A duffer

indicators.note: the word boy is thrown out of the word bossy, as a pupil is expelled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A domineering pupil thrown out of school, written off as a dunce.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B, O and Y from BOSSY leaves SS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fool or dimwit is called a donkey-name, the same word as a duffer.

clue.text: Don't allow to torment and jeer

parts.note: to bar is to forbid or not allow
to rack is to torture or torment

explanation.surface: A plea to stop bullies tormenting and mocking someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to heckle or shout abuse at a performer or player.

clue.text: And in darts playing it's the norm

indicators.note: playing suggests moving about freely, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: In pub darts this is the usual practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is the accepted norm or benchmark by which things are judged.

clue.text: Leaves bundled up, prepared for a dowsing

definitions.text: Leaves bundled up, prepared for a dowsing

parts.words: Leaves bundled up, prepared for a dowsing
parts.note: tea leaves packed into a little porous pouch, ready to have boiling water poured over them

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' sounds like foliage and 'dowsing' like water-divining, but these are tea leaves about to be doused.
explanation.definitionFit: A small sachet of tea leaves is steeped in hot water, so it is soaked: a cryptic description.

clue.text: Badly needs to get hold of: one refuses

indicators.note: getting hold of something means grasping it, so the jumbled letters enclose the numeral
badly signals the letters of needs are put in a poor, disordered arrangement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone in dire need tries to grab hold of something, but is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges NEEDS as DENES, which takes in I.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'he denies' means he refuses or rejects; the verb form fits 'one refuses'.

clue.text: Not 'The Ballad of Reading Gaol'?

parts.note: Oscar Wilde's poem written after prison uses strict rhyme and metre, and its author was not at liberty

explanation.walkthrough: Wilde's poem about Reading prison is rhymed and metred, and he had been locked up; poetry without rules is the opposite, both unrestricted and unconfined.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry with no fixed rhyme or metre is unconstrained, the reverse of a gaol ballad by a prisoner.

clue.text: Not that plus that makes a star!

definitions.text: Not that plus that makes a star!

parts.words: Not that plus that makes a star!
parts.note: plus is a synonym of the answer, and a film's background performer is the opposite of its lead

explanation.walkthrough: The word means 'plus' or 'additional', and in films it is a walk-on player, someone who is definitely not a star.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit-part film player has no lines and is far from the lead, while the word also means additional.

clue.text: Act One is set in a foreign city

indicators.note: the numeral is set in the other word, placed inside it

parts.note: a turn is an act in a variety show
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Theatre notes: the opening act takes place in an overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: Turin is a major city in northern Italy, home of Juventus and Fiat.

clue.text: Part and at embarkation point I get aboard

parts.note: a port is where ships are boarded, the point of embarkation
being aboard a vehicle is being on it

explanation.surface: A traveller explains how they boarded a ship at the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is a share or part of a whole, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Bit it clear off at top end

indicators.note: the end of the word top is its final letter
off means gone wrong or out of place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone bit off a clear piece at the top end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end' takes the last letter of top, P, placed at the top (front); 'off' rearranges ITCLEAR as ARTICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny piece or speck, so a small bit.

clue.text: Ask to get dead identified and returned

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogy
to be identified is to be named

explanation.surface: Requesting that a body be identified and sent home.
explanation.definitionFit: To demand is to ask for something firmly, insisting on it.
